chapter_title: The Agent Loop, Tools, and Context
learning_objective: The learner will explain what the harness does after each of 6 model replies or tool results by choosing the outcome of each, with at least 5 of 6 correct.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** agent-loop-stepper
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/ai-strategy-for-education/tree/main/docs/sims/ai-agent-anatomy
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** explain
**Learning Objective:** The learner will explain what the harness does after each of 6 model replies or tool results by choosing the outcome of each, with at least 5 of 6 correct. **Prerequisites:** AI agent harness, agent loop, agent turn, tool definition, permission model, context compaction, context truncation (all defined in the sections above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner first steps once through the five phases of one turn. The learner then answers 6 situations by choosing one of the six outcomes before any answer is revealed. A choice is correct when it equals the Correct outcome column. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Stepping through is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The model runs its own tools. (2) A tool call written as text still runs. (3) The conversation is reset each turn. (4) A permission question is answered automatically. **Instructional Rationale:** Explaining a mechanism needs the learner to predict its behavior in cases that differ in one detail, so each situation changes a single fact about the reply or the result, and the outcomes are the possible next states of the loop. **Content:** The five phases of one turn, shown as the learner steps through them: 1. The harness sends the whole conversation to the model. 2. The model writes a reply. 3. The harness checks the reply for a tool call. 4. If there is one, the harness checks the permission rules and runs the tool. 5. The harness appends the reply and the result to the conversation, and the loop starts again. The six outcomes the learner chooses from: "The harness runs the tool, appends the result, and calls the model again", "The loop ends and the reply is returned", "The harness sees no tool call and the loop ends early", "The conversation grows by the size of the result", "The harness compacts or truncates earlier content", and "The run stalls waiting for an approval". | # | Situation shown to the learner | Correct outcome | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | The reply contains a well-formed request to read a file. | The harness runs the tool, appends the result, and calls the model again | A tool call is exactly what the loop acts on. | | 2 | The reply is a finished answer with no tool call. | The loop ends and the reply is returned | With no tool call the loop has nothing to run. | | 3 | The reply writes the tool call out as plain text inside its answer. | The harness sees no tool call and the loop ends early | Only a structured request is a tool call, so the text is treated as a final reply. | | 4 | A shell command returns 8,000 tokens of output. | The conversation grows by the size of the result | The result is appended, so every later turn reads it. | | 5 | The conversation is about to exceed the model's window. | The harness compacts or truncates earlier content | The conversation has to shrink to fit, by summary or by dropping the oldest content. | | 6 | A permission rule requires approval for the tool and nobody is present. | The run stalls waiting for an approval | An unattended run cannot answer, so it waits. | **Provenance:** The situations are synthetic, written for this exercise, and the sim labels them "synthetic example". The mechanism comes from the sections of this chapter above. **Rules:** Situations are shown in the fixed order 1 to 6. Each allows one final choice, and exactly one outcome is correct for each situation. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner presses Next to move through the five phases of one turn, with the conversation shown growing at phase 5. 2. After phase 5 the learner begins the six situations and reads situation 1. 3. The learner chooses one of the six outcomes and confirms. 4. The sim shows the correct outcome and the Why text, and marks the situation correct or incorrect. 5. After situation 6 the sim shows the score and the misconception behind each miss. **Feedback:** Six situations, fixed order, one confirmed choice each, no second attempt. Correct: "Correct" followed by the Why text. Incorrect: "Not quite" followed by the correct outcome and the Why text. The final score reads "n of 6 correct". **Starting State:** The loop is shown at phase 1 with a short conversation, and the question on screen is "What does the harness do with the model's reply?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter states that a tool call written as plain text ends the loop, that a tool result is appended and read by every later turn, that an approval rule stalls an unattended run, and that a conversation near the window is compacted or truncated.
